text:
emily: Heads-up — ran a concurrency sweep against the new q4-int8 runner for the onboarding model and saw p95 latency jump from ~220ms to ~640ms around 480qps. cost/token also spiked ~2x.
rahul: huh. did you warm up the KV cache? the harness default warmup uses short prompts, might not prime prefix KV properly.
maria: confirming — the CI warmup job uses `--warmup-samples 20 --prefix='Hello'` which is not representative for this model (longer instruction tokens). I can paste the job snippet.
emily: pls paste. i suspected warmup mismatch because the first-window latencies are normal then regress after a few mins.
maria: snippet:
```
./eval-runner --model onb-v1-q4 --concurrency 512 --warmup-samples 20 \ 
  --prefix "Hello" --batch-window-ms 10
```
emily: ^ that's it. our real traffic has repeated long prefixes (300-600 tokens) so KV eviction/regen cost shows up in steady-state. CI warmup is underpriming the KV cache.
rahul: two options: (1) change harness warmup to replay a representative prefix set, or (2) enable aggressive kv-prefetch during warmup (cheap but risks masking regen bugs). i prefer (1) for correctness.
sara: for quick mitigation, can we lower the canary SLO alert so paging doesn't trigger? we need to avoid paged ops during the rollout.
emily: proposing changes:
- update eval-harness warmup to replay session traces (use /tests/onboarding/prefixes.json)
- add `--kv-prefetch true` as a transient flag for night runs
- update dashboard alert p95 -> 700ms temporary
rahul: sounds good. i'll take the harness patch and add an integration test ensuring warmup traces produce the same kvcache hit rate as production logs. @maria can you add the prefixes artifact to the testdata bundle?
maria: adding prefixes.json in the runner artifacts now. also adding a tiny test that asserts kvcache_hit_rate >= 0.85 after warmup.
ci-bot: eveval-1873 warmup-run started (job 5421) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
emily: thanks. once the harness change lands we'll rerun the sweep and check p95 + cost/token. if still bad we dig into batch-windowing interactions.
rahul: note: batch-window-ms=10 may amplify regen if kvcache isn't primed. we'll keep window at 5ms for the canary.
sara: i'll temporarily relax the oncall paging threshold and note the incident in the rollout doc. :white_check_mark:
emily: ok rolling this into a small canary: patch -> canary -> metrics-check -> global rollout. thanks all :rocket:
